COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
WPSS No.369 of 2023
Hon 'b le Man oj Ku m ar Tiw ar i, J.

Mr. Avidit Noliyal, Advocate for the
petitioner.
Mr. Puran Singh Bisht, Additional
C.S.C. for the State of Uttarakhand.
Mr. Bhagwat Mehra, Advocate for
respondent nos. 2 & 3.
Heard learned counsel for the parties.
 Petitioner's father was employed as
T.G.-1 in Uttarakhand Power Corporation
Ltd., who died while in service on
31.07.2022. Petitioner has applied for
com passionate appointment. Since no
decision has been taken on his application,
therefore, he has approached this Court.
Learned counsel for respondent nos. 2
& 3, however, points out that petitioner's
father had m arried second tim e after death
of petitioner's mother and the second wife
of late Prem Lal Tam ta has also applied for
com passionate appointment. He further
points out that the stepmother of
petitioner has three minor children,
therefore, it is not possible to give
com passionate appointm ent to the
petitioner in the absence of any
adjudication on the rights of the parties.
He further points out that initially a
com promise entered between petitioner
and his stepm other was filed on
15.09.2022 before Competent Authority in
U.P.C.L., however, subsequently,
petitioner's stepm other backed out and
submitted a comm unication on 02.11.2022
that she does not abide by the
com promise.

Learned counsel for the petitioner has
drawn attention of this Court to Rule 7 of
U.P. Recruitm ent of Dependants of
Government Servants Dying-in-Harness
Rules, 1974, which reads as under:
 "7 . Procedure when m ore than one m em ber of the
fam ily seeks em ploym ent. - If m ore than one m em ber of
the fam ily of the deceased Governm ent servant seeks
em ploym ent under these rules, the Head of Office shall
decide about the suitability of the person for giving
em ploym ent. The decision will be taken keeping in view also
the overall interest of the welfare of the entire fam ily,
particularly the widow and the m inor m em bers thereof."
Based on Rule 7, learned counsel for
the petitioner submits that in case of
dispute between two or m ore m em bers,
Competent Authority has to decide
suitability of the person for giving
em ploym ent. Thus, he submits that the
inaction on the part of the Com petent
Authority in taking decision on com peting
claim of petitioner and his stepm other, is
unjust.
This Court finds som e substance in
the contention m ade by learned counsel
for the petitioner. Since Rule 7 provides
for adjudication of com peting claim s
between two or m ore family m em bers,
therefore, the writ petition is disposed of
with a direction to Com petent Authority in
U.P.C.L. to examine the claim of petitioner
and his stepmother and take appropriate
decision, as per law, within a period of ten
weeks' from the date of production of
certified copy of this order.
I t goes without saying that, before
taking any decision, petitioner and his
stepm other shall be given personal hearing
by the Com petent Authority.

( Man oj Ku m ar Tiw ar i, J.)
 16.03.2023
